T2_closure.value: T2 is suitable as a secondary, confidence-aware priority prediction signal within the integrated IT Ticket Intelligence system. It should assist triage and downstream evidence fusion, but should not independently determine final ticket priority.
The prediction boundary is Creation, preserving the intended incoming-ticket decision boundary.
Overall five-class predictive performance is limited: final test accuracy is 42.0113% and macro-F1 is 26.4960%.
A universal automated confidence threshold has not been empirically established.
T2 can contribute one evidence channel to a larger confidence-aware triage system.
T2 does not support automatic action at a fixed confidence threshold without further empirical calibration and policy evaluation.
T2 does not establish that predicted priority should replace human priority judgment.

Mozilla CORE is suitable for T2 priority-prediction modeling under the frozen Creation-time target and feature boundary. The final TF-IDF + Class-Weighted Logistic Regression model demonstrates measurable but limited predictive performance on the locked chronological test period. Because minority-class performance is weak and generalization degrades on the later period, T2 is closed as a supported secondary decision-support signal rather than an autonomous priority assignment component.
Retain the T2 prediction as one evidence channel for later confidence-aware fusion and human-review policy development. Do not independently automate final priority assignment from T2.

T3_closure.value: DistilBERT achieved higher accuracy and weighted F1 in feasibility testing but lower macro F1 and did not resolve S1/S2 detection.
Use T3 severity prediction as a secondary decision-support signal for downstream triage or human review. Do not treat the prediction as an autonomous or authoritative severity assignment.

T3 — Severity Prediction is CLOSED as a SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITATIONS secondary decision-support signal. The selected candidate is T3-MOD-008 under the pre-frozen macro-F1 criterion. Locked test evaluation and final generalization analysis are complete. The task is not treated as an autonomous severity assignment capability.
